marks.gloss_en: מאי טעמא? אמר רבא, בר המדורי אסברה לי: the mat is fit to cover dirt, and its shreds to cover filth
Shmuel: reed shreds of a mat may be moved on Shabbat
אלא אמר רב פפא: אם זרקה מבעוד יום לאשפה -- אסורה (= p_rp_mibeod_yom_asur)
Rav Pappa: if he threw it on the dump while it was still day [before Shabbat], it is forbidden
Rav: remnants of cloaks may not be moved on Shabbat
a stone in a gourd: if one fills with it and [the stone] does not fall, one may fill with it
כמאן -- כרבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the practice rests on his testimony that an oven cover needs no handle
R' Eliezer b. Yaakov (as R' Yosei testified): shards of an old oven may be moved on Shabbat
ורבי מאיר לטעמיה -- R' Meir follows his line in the shards mishna: some kind of work suffices
ואזדא רבי יהודה לטעמיה -- R' Yehuda follows his line in the shards mishna: work like their own is required
Abaye: they dispute shards that do some kind of work but not work like their own
דתנן: נתנו על פי הבור... -- the Kelim mishna in which R' Yehuda holds such an oven is no vessel (no support kind names דתנן)
Rava: they dispute the shards of THIS oven [the one of the mishna, set over a pit]
כדרב יהודה אמר שמואל: מחלוקת בהיסק ראשון, אבל בהיסק שני אפילו תלוי בצואר גמל
ואידך נמי, הכתיב טמאים יהיו לכם! -- and for the other too, is 'they shall be impure to you' not written?
ההיא כדרב יהודה אמר שמואל -- that verse is as Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel's name (= p_ry_temeim_heseik_sheni)
for R' Yehuda, 'they shall be impure to you' is [about the second firing], as Rav Yehuda said in Shmuel's name
מתקיף לה רבא: אי הכי, אדמיפלגי בשברי תנור ליפלגו בשברי כלים בעלמא -- if so, instead of disputing oven shards, let them dispute ordinary shards
לעולם כדאמרן מעיקרא ובעושה מעשה טפקא -- the dispute is set in the tapka case, where R' Meir argues on R' Yehuda's own terms (= p_rav_ashi_tapka, p_rm_aliba_ry_tapka)
Rav Ashi: really as we said at first, and [the dispute is] where he makes a tapka with them

מתקיף לה רב אשי: אי הכי, ליפלגו בתנור גופה -- השתא תנור גופה לרבי יהודה לא הוי מנא, שבריו מיבעיא? -- let them dispute the oven itself; if the oven itself is no vessel for R' Yehuda, need its shards be said?
ורבנן נמי, הכתיב יותץ? -- and for the Rabbis too, is 'it shall be smashed' not written?
ההוא לאידך גיסא -- it comes for the other side: lest one think an oven attached to the ground is like the ground (= p_rabbanan_yutatz_lo_karka)
for the Rabbis, 'it shall be smashed' teaches the other side: you might think that since he attached it to the ground it is like the ground itself -- it teaches us otherwise
ורבי יהודה: לא דמי -- R' Yehuda (as Rav Ashi presents him) refuses the concession: the tapka is fired from without and does not stand
R' Yehuda: it is not similar -- there it is fired from within, here from without; there it stands, here it does not
the shards of an old oven may be moved, like all vessels moved in a courtyard
the stam: they dispute over this verse -- 'oven or stove, it shall be smashed; they are impure and shall be impure to you' (Lev 11:35)
Ulla: and the first firing, for the Rabbis -- even if it hangs on a camel's neck [it is impure]
